The one thing the body flagged as non-trivial (the coverage constraint) is
resolved by measurement, not by a user decision. Findings below.

## Context resolved

Sources consulted: `.claude/rules/*.md` frontmatter (all 43 on-demand rules),
`scripts/workflow_lint.py` (`check_rule_frontmatter_parses`, ~L13605-13690),
`.claude/rules/LESSONS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (Upload Policy + marker Critical Rules),
`tests/test_workflow_lint.py`, and a content scan of all 1,387 `scripts/issue*.py`.

**1. The premise is confirmed exactly.** Three rules carry `scripts/issue*.py`:
`upload-policy.md` (59,919 B), `marker-leakage-measurement.md` (17,089 B),
`marker-training-recipe.md` (14,782 B) = 91,790 B. `scripts/issue*.py` matches
all 1,387 issue scripts.

**2. Measured load-set correction.** For the named plotter
`scripts/issue1336_full_transfer_lattice.py` the ON-DEMAND RULE load-set is
125,629 B across 4 rules (the 3 above + `code-style.md` at 33,839 B, which is
legitimate for a `.py` touch). The body's 453,305 B figure is the whole
always-on stack, not the rule load-set; the narrowable portion is 91,790 B =
**73% of this file's on-demand rule load**. Post-fix that file would load
33,839 B (code-style only). `gotchas.md` (181,576 B) does NOT match — its globs
are already narrow.

**3. Filename globs CANNOT separate the bearing subsets — this kills suggested
direction (2).** Content scan of all 1,387 issue scripts:

| bearing class | scripts | of which the FILENAME carries the token |
|---|---|---|
| upload (`upload_folder`/`upload_file`/`HfApi`/`huggingface_hub`/`create_commit`) | 457 | 18 |
| marker (`MARKER_TEXT`/`83399`/the marker glyph/`marker_logprob`) | 90 | 5 |
| train (`SFTTrainer`/`Trainer(`/`train_lora`/`LoraConfig`/`get_peft_model`) | 31 | 5 |

Narrowing to name-shaped globs (`scripts/*train*.py`, `scripts/*upload*.py`)
would drop the deep rule for 439 of 457 upload-bearing scripts — a ~96%
coverage regression, exactly the safety regression the body forbids.

**4. Content-keyed triggering is NOT available — this kills direction (3).**
`workflow_lint.py` L13605-13611 states the mechanism outright: a rule
"on-demand-loads ONLY through its frontmatter `paths:` globs." The validated
schema is a non-empty YAML list of glob strings; there is no content predicate.

**5. The summary tier the body asks for in direction (1) ALREADY EXISTS and is
already always-on.** `CLAUDE.md` § "Upload Policy" carries the artifact
destination table plus the core rules (persist-by-default, text-always,
never-delete-unuploaded, verify-before-terminate) and explicitly labels the rule
file as "Deep mechanics"; the marker Critical Rules bullet carries the load-
bearing dial (lr ≤5e-6, marker-at-end on-policy DV, three-space reporting) and
names both marker rules; `LESSONS.md` — always-on by `@`-import — indexes all
three with plan-time triggers under an explicit "trigger matches => open +
follow the rule" contract. So the floor of coverage does not come from the glob,
and narrowing the DEEP tier does not remove it. This is the finding that makes
the fix tractable rather than a safety trade.

**6. Mechanical constraints are loose.** `--check-rule-frontmatter-parses`
validates frontmatter SHAPE only (parses, non-`globs:`, non-empty string list) —
it does not constrain glob CONTENT. No test in `tests/` pins these globs. So the
edit is mechanically free; the entire risk is the coverage judgment in (3)/(5).

## The one open design fork (planner-owned, not user-blocking)

Given (3) and (4), the only reachable designs are variants of "narrow the deep
tier and lean on the already-always-on summary tier" (5). The residual choice —
how narrow, and whether to add an explicit high-value allow-list of the
dispatcher/train/upload scripts that genuinely carry the mechanics — is a scope
call the body itself delegates ("Suggested directions (not prescriptive — the
plan owns the choice)"), and per `.claude/rules/auto-continuation.md` a
scope/design-preference call is never a block in an autonomous session. The plan
resolves it with the enumerations in (3) as evidence.
